attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) to serve DHCP on lan-a (eth2, the discovered link to node3) handing out 10.10.1.100-200/24 with itself (10.10.1.1) as default router, and node2 (OPNsense) to serve DHCP on lan-b (vtnet2, the discovered link to node4) handing out 10.10.2.100-200/24 with itself (10.10.2.1) as default router. node3 and node4's second NICs were switched from unconfigured/static to NetworkManager DHCP-client profiles and now obtain address plus default route dynamically from their respective router. All four nodes were then restarted one at a time; each showed a changed boot identity and fully recovered DHCP service/lease state and connectivity afterward.
